question.text: A cubical solid aluminum <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mrow><mi>bulk</mi><mo> </mo><mi>modulus</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mi>V</mi><mfrac><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">d</mi><mi>P</mi></mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">d</mi><mi>V</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>70</mn><mo> </mo><mi>GPa</mi></mrow></mfenced></math> block has an edge length of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> on the surface of the earth. It is kept on the floor of a <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi>km</mi></math> deep ocean. Taking the average density of water and the acceleration due to gravity to be <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>3</mn></msup><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>, respectively, the change in the edge length of the block in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>mm</mi></math> is ________.
